name: Google Assistant
tagline: Google Assistant is giving way to Gemini on Android. GAIA replaces it for reminders, email, calendar and tasks.
painPoints: Being deprecated in favor of Gemini; future uncertain for power users
Primarily voice-focused; limited for complex text-based workflows
No desktop or professional productivity integration beyond basics
Cannot manage professional email, complex task lists, or work calendars
Privacy concerns with always-on microphone and Google data processing
metaTitle: Google Assistant Alternative: A Replacement for Android
metaDescription: Google Assistant is giving way to Gemini. GAIA works on Android via the web app and chat apps, and handles email, calendar, and reminders. See how to switch.
whyPeopleLook:
Google is replacing Google Assistant with Gemini on Android phones, and on phones that have switched, "Hey Google" now opens Gemini. That is what replaced Google Assistant for most people. Some users miss what Assistant did well, such as quick device commands, routines and smart home control; others want an assistant that does more real work than either. If you are looking for a Google Assistant alternative on Android, first decide which job you need covered.

For phone-level voice control (the hotword, alarms, phone settings, smart home devices) you need an app that Android lets you set as the default digital assistant. Gemini is the obvious one, and on most phones you can see which installed apps qualify under Settings, Apps, Default apps. GAIA is not that kind of app: it does not answer the hotword or change phone settings.

For professional productivity, Google Assistant was always limited: it could set timers and read calendar events, but could not triage email, manage complex task lists, or run multi-step workflows. GAIA fills that gap. On Android you use it in the browser (the web app also has a voice mode) or by messaging it on Telegram or WhatsApp. It works deeply with Gmail and Google Calendar, remembers context across conversations, sends reminders, and runs workflows in the background.
gaiaReplaces: Calendar event creation and scheduling via natural language
Email reading and drafting with full Gmail integration
Reminder and task creation from conversation
Daily briefings covering email, tasks, and calendar
Cross-platform assistant available on mobile, desktop, and bots
gaiaAdvantages: Not being deprecated: source-available and actively developed
Professional productivity focus beyond voice commands
Proactive monitoring of email and calendar without asking
Self-hostable for complete privacy and data control
Works in the web app (including on phone browsers), the desktop app, and through Discord, Slack, Telegram and WhatsApp
migrationSteps: Connect GAIA to Gmail for email management
Link Google Calendar for meeting and scheduling assistance
Set up GAIA's daily briefing to replace morning Google Assistant summaries
Use GAIA on your phone via the web app or chat bots for on-the-go queries and task management
Recreate your Assistant reminders by asking GAIA in plain English, for example "remind me every Monday at 9 to send the timesheet"
Keep Gemini or another default assistant app for the hotword, phone settings and smart home control

faqs.question: Can GAIA replace Google Assistant for reminders?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA can set reminders, create tasks, and send follow-up notifications. It goes further by setting reminders intelligently based on your email and calendar context.

faqs.question: Does GAIA work on Android like Google Assistant?
faqs.answer: GAIA works on Android and iOS through the web app and chat bots. It does not integrate with Android system features like assistant shortcuts, but provides a full-featured productivity assistant experience.

faqs.question: Is GAIA a good replacement now that Google Assistant is being retired?
faqs.answer: For professional productivity tasks (email, calendar, tasks, and workflow automation), GAIA is a strong replacement. For smart home control, you would still need a Google Home hub or a separate smart home platform.

faqs.question: Does GAIA respect privacy better than Google Assistant?
faqs.answer: GAIA is source-available and self-hostable, meaning your data can stay entirely on your own servers. Unlike Google Assistant, GAIA does not require an always-on microphone.

faqs.question: What replaced Google Assistant?
faqs.answer: On Android phones, Google is replacing Google Assistant with Gemini, its AI assistant; on phones that have switched, "Hey Google" opens Gemini, and Google is moving other devices to Gemini as well. If you want an alternative focused on email, calendar and tasks rather than device control, GAIA covers that side.

faqs.question: What is the best Google Assistant alternative for Android?
faqs.answer: It depends on the job. For hands-free device control and the hotword, use an app Android accepts as the default digital assistant, such as Gemini. For running your work (triaging Gmail, scheduling on Google Calendar, reminders, follow-ups and workflows), GAIA goes further than Assistant ever did; on Android you use it in the browser or through Telegram and WhatsApp.

faqs.question: Can I set GAIA as my default assistant on Android?
faqs.answer: No. GAIA does not register as an Android digital assistant app, so it cannot answer "Hey Google" or open from the power button. Add the GAIA web app to your home screen from your browser, or message GAIA on Telegram or WhatsApp instead.
